theorem.content:
\label{thm:trace_periodicity} 
    Let $N\geq 1$ and let $H$ be a subgroup
    of $\mathrm{GL}_2(\mathbb Z/N\mathbb Z)$.
    Let $\ell$ be a prime and if $H$ is not representable then let $\ell \geq 5$. Let $q=p^a$ be a prime power with $\gcd(q,N)=1$. 
    Let $s \geq 1$, and  
    \[
    k_0 = \begin{cases} s-1 & \text{if } \ell \neq p; \\ s & \text{if } \ell = p \neq q; \\
    2s-1 & \text{if } \ell = p = q.
    \end{cases}
    \]
    \noindent If $k \geq k_0$ then   
    \[
    \Tr(F_q \, | \, S[H,k+2]) + \epsilon_k \equiv_{\ell^s} \Tr(F_q \, | \, S[H,k+2+n]),
    \]
    where 
    \[
    n =
    \begin{cases}
    \ell^{s-1}(\ell^2-1) & \text{if } \ell\geq 3 \text{ and }  \left( \frac{q}{\ell} \right) = -1 ; \\
    \ell^{s}(\ell^2-1)/2 & \text{if } \ell\geq 3 \text{ and } \left( \frac{q}{\ell} \right) = 1;\\
    \ell^{s}(\ell^2-1) & \text{if } \ell=2 \text{ and } q \text{ is a non-square mod } \ell^s; \\
    \text{lcm}(2,\ell^{s-1}(\ell^2-1)) & \text{if } \ell=2 \text{ and } q \text{ is an odd square mod } \ell^s; \\
    \ell^{s-1}(\ell-1) & \text{if } \ell = p, 
    \end{cases}
    \]
     and where $\epsilon_k=0$ for any $k>0$ and $\epsilon_0=-(q+1) \Tr(F_q \, | \, H_c^0(\mathcal X_H\otimes \overline{\mathbb{F}}_q))$ with
     $\mathcal X_H$ the compact modular curve with level structure $H$.  

    If $H$ is not representable and $\ell=2$ or $3$, then the above statement holds but with $s$ replaced by $s+\nu_\ell(H,q)$ in the definition of $n$. 
    In the case $\ell=2$ and $-\mathrm{Id}\in H$ then $s$ can instead be replaced by $s+\nu_2(H,q)-1$ in the definition of~$n$.
theorem.label: thm:trace_periodicity

sketch:
In Remark after Theorem~\ref{thm:trace_periodicity}, under the special assumptions $\Gamma=\Gamma(N)$ with $N\ge 3$, $q=p\ne \ell$, $s=1$, and $k>\ell+1$, one uses Serre’s congruence for
\[
 w_k=\Tr(F_p\,|\,S[\Gamma,k])-\Tr(F_p\,|\,S[\Gamma,k-(\ell-1)])
\]
that $w_{k+\ell+1}\equiv_{\ell} p\cdot w_k$. From this it follows that
\[
 w_{k+\ell^2-1}\equiv_{\ell} p^{\ell-1}w_k\equiv_{\ell} w_k,
\]
and then
\begin{multline*}
\Tr(F_p\,|\,S[\Gamma,k+\ell(\ell^2-1)])-\Tr(F_p\,|\,S[\Gamma,k])\\
\equiv_{\ell} \sum_{i=0}^{\ell} \sum_{j=0}^{\ell-1} w_{k+(\ell-1)((\ell+1)(\ell-j)-i)}
\equiv_{\ell} \sum_{i=0}^{\ell}\ell\cdot w_{k+(\ell-1)(\ell+1-i)}\equiv_{\ell}0,
\end{multline*}
which yields a periodicity of traces mod $\ell$.

If $p$ is a square mod $\ell\ne 2$, then similarly $w_{k+(\ell^2-1)/2}\equiv_{\ell} w_k$ and
\begin{multline*}
\Tr(F_p\,|\,S[\Gamma,k+\ell(\ell^2-1)/2])-\Tr(F_p\,|\,S[\Gamma,k])\\
\equiv_{\ell} \sum_{i=0}^{(\ell-1)/2} \sum_{j=0}^{\ell-1} w_{k+(\ell-1)((\ell+1)(\ell-j)/2-i)}
\equiv_{\ell} \sum_{i=0}^{(\ell-1)/2}\ell\cdot w_{k+(\ell-1)((\ell+1)/2-i)}\equiv_{\ell}0.
\end{multline*}
The remark concludes: “This shows periodicities as in Theorem~\ref{thm:trace_periodicity}, but with a slightly larger period if $p$ is a non-square mod~$\ell$.”

mcq.question:
Let $N\ge 1$ and let $H\le \mathrm{GL}_2(\mathbb Z/N\mathbb Z)$. Let $\ell$ be a prime (and if $H$ is not representable, assume $\ell\ge 5$). Let $q=p^a$ be a prime power with $\gcd(q,N)=1$, and let $s\ge 1$. Define
\[
 k_0=\begin{cases}
 s-1 & \text{if }\ell\neq p,\\
 s & \text{if }\ell=p\neq q,\\
 2s-1 & \text{if }\ell=p=q.
 \end{cases}
\]
For an integer $k\ge k_0$, what is the strongest guaranteed congruence modulo $\ell^s$ relating $\mathrm{Tr}(F_q\mid S[H,k+2])$ and $\mathrm{Tr}(F_q\mid S[H,k+2+n])$, including the exact piecewise definition of $n$ and the correction term $\epsilon_k$ (and indicating the stated modification when $H$ is not representable and $\ell\in\{2,3\}$)?

correct_choice.label: A
correct_choice.text:
For every integer $k\ge k_0$,
\[
\Tr(F_q\mid S[H,k+2]) + \epsilon_k \equiv \Tr(F_q\mid S[H,k+2+n]) \pmod{\ell^s},
\]
where
\[
 n=
 \begin{cases}
 \ell^{s-1}(\ell^2-1) & \text{if } \ell\ge 3 \text{ and } \left(\frac{q}{\ell}\right)=-1,\\
 \ell^{s}(\ell^2-1)/2 & \text{if } \ell\ge 3 \text{ and } \left(\frac{q}{\ell}\right)=1,\\
 \ell^{s}(\ell^2-1) & \text{if } \ell=2 \text{ and } q \text{ is a non-square mod } \ell^s,\\
 \mathrm{lcm}\bigl(2,\ell^{s-1}(\ell^2-1)\bigr) & \text{if } \ell=2 \text{ and } q \text{ is an odd square mod } \ell^s,\\
 \ell^{s-1}(\ell-1) & \text{if } \ell=p,
 \end{cases}
\]
and
\[\epsilon_k=0\ \text{for }k>0,\qquad \epsilon_0=-(q+1)\Tr\bigl(F_q\mid H_c^0(\mathcal X_H\otimes \overline{\mathbb F}_q)\bigr),\]

theorem.content:
\label{main}
There exists a simple closed geodesic $\gamma_\infty(u)=(r(u),x(u))$, $u\in\mathbb{S}^1$,
in the half-plane $(\mathbb{R}^2_+,g)$.
Moreover, its length $L_g(\gamma_\infty)$ with respect to the metric $g$
is less than the length of the double cover of the half-line $x=0$.
theorem.label: main

post_theorem_intro_text:
Note that Drugan-Nguyen  \cite{Drugan&Nguyen} 
proved Theorem \ref{main} for the case when $\lambda=n-1$.
In fact, the proof of Theorem \ref{main} closely follows that of \cite{Drugan&Nguyen}.
We also remark that, similar to the case when $\lambda=n-1$,  
we do not know whether
the $\lambda$-Angenent curve constructed in Theorem \ref{main}
coincides with the one  constructed by the shooting method.

L_g(\gamma_\infty) < L_g(\text{the double cover of the half-line }x=0).
\]

\[
L_g(\gamma_\infty) \le L_g(\text{the double cover of the half-line }x=0).
\]

choices.text:

\[
L_g(\gamma_\infty) < L_g(x=0).
\]

    $$\#\mathscr{E}_{f,\mathfrak{n}}(X)=(\mathrm{N}_{K/\mathbb{Q}}(\mathfrak{n}))^{n-d}\exp\left({O\left(\frac{\log\mathrm{N}_{K/\mathbb{Q}}(\mathfrak{n})}{\log\log\mathrm{N}_{K/\mathbb{Q}}(\mathfrak{n})}\right)}\right).$$
    The implied constant in the $O$-terms depends only on $K,X$ and $f$.
\end{theorem}

Although Theorem \ref{approximate} provides an asymptotic bound for general smooth varieties, the error term can be significantly improved when the variety $X$ has low degree. Since previous studies have focused mostly on linear and quadratic congruences as discussed before, we derive the following sharper estimate for the varieties of degree no more than 2. 

\begin{theorem}\label{approximate 2}
     Given a number field $K$ with ring of integers $\mathcal{O}_K$, let $f\in \mathcal{O}_K[x]$ be a polynomial. Let $X$ be a smooth closed subvariety of $\mathbb{A}^n_{\mathcal{O}_K}$ with $\mathrm{codim}(X)=d$ and $\mathrm{deg}X\le 2$, which is geometrically irreducible over K. For a nonzero integral ideal $\mathfrak{n}$ of $\mathcal{O}_K$ such that $X$ has a good reduction at $\mathfrak{p}$ for any prime ideal $\mathfrak{p}\vert \mathfrak{n}$, we have$$\#\mathscr{E}_{f,\mathfrak{n}}(X)=\mathrm{N}_{K/\mathbb{Q}}(\mathfrak{n})^{n-d}\left(
\log \mathrm{N}_{K/\mathbb{Q}}(\mathfrak{n})\right)^{O(1)}.$$
The implied constant in the $O$-terms depends only on $K,X$ and $f$.
\end{theorem}

Our approach relies on the multiplicative structure of the counting function derived from the Chinese Remainder Theorem in Dedekind domains. For the counting functions in the local case, we employ a Hensel-type technique to lift solutions from the residue field $\mathcal{O}_K/\mathfrak{p}$ to $\mathcal{O}_K/\mathfrak{p}^k$. To establish the asymptotic estimate for $\#\mathscr{E}_{f,\mathfrak{n}}(X)$, we use the well-known Lang-Weil inequality to control the error terms arising from the local points on the variety.

This paper is organized as follows.

In Section \ref{proof of main}, we provide the proof of Theorem \ref{main}. The argument begins with establishing the multiplicativity of the counting function $\#\mathscr{E}_{f,\mathfrak{n}}(X)$ via the Chinese Remainder Theorem. Then we derived these local counting formulas by using Hensel lifting. To illustrate the concrete application of our counting formula, we present a detailed example involving a given variety $X$ over the quadratic field $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{-5})$ at the end of this section.

In Section \ref{proof of approximation}, we focus on the asymptotic behavior of $\#\mathscr{E}_{f,\mathfrak{n}}(X)$ as the norm of the ideal $N(\mathfrak{n})$ tends to infinity. Using the Lang-Weil inequality, we derive a general estimate for the number of $(f,\mathfrak{n})$-exunits, which depends on the dimension and degree of the variety and the absolute norm of $\mathfrak{n}$. Furthermore, we investigate the specific case where $\deg X \le 2$. Noting that the leading error term coefficient vanishes for quadratic varieties and linear varieties, we obtain a refined estimate that improves the error bound from $\exp\left({O\left(\frac{\log\mathrm{N}_{K/\mathbb{Q}}(\mathfrak{n})}{\log\log\mathrm{N}_{K/\mathbb{Q}}(\mathfrak{n})}\right)}\right)$ to $\exp\left(
O(\log\log \mathrm{N}_{K/\mathbb{Q}}(\mathfrak{n}))
\right)=\left(
\log \mathrm{N}_{K/\mathbb{Q}}(\mathfrak{n})\right)^{O(1)}$.

\label{thm:slowscanning}
The scanning algorithm and the divide-and-conquer algorithm of \cite{MR2320156} run in exponential time with respect to the number of crossings in a link diagram, even when restricted to positive $3$-braids, or to alternating $3$-braids.
theorem.label: thm:slowscanning

sketch: The post-theorem text explains that the exponential runtime in Theorem~\ref{thm:slowscanning} comes from the existence of $3$-braids whose total Betti numbers grow exponentially with the number of crossings. Consequently, “Any algorithm, which works with a basis on the chain complex, will therefore necessarily have an exponential runtime.” It also notes that these “exponential Betti numbers” obstruct polynomial-time accuracy for the main quantum algorithm of \cite{schmidhuber2025quantumalgorithmkhovanovhomology} on $3$-braids.

mcq.question: Consider the scanning algorithm and the divide-and-conquer algorithm of \cite{MR2320156} applied to link diagrams. Even when the input diagrams are restricted to be positive $3$-braids or to be alternating $3$-braids, what is the strongest general statement guaranteed about these algorithms' running time as a function of the number of crossings in the diagram?

correct_choice.text: Both the scanning algorithm and the divide-and-conquer algorithm run in exponential time with respect to the number of crossings in the link diagram, even when restricted to positive $3$-braids or to alternating $3$-braids.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Both the scanning algorithm and the divide-and-conquer algorithm of \cite{MR2320156} run in \emph{subexponential} time (e.g. $2^{o(c)}$) with respect to the number of crossings $c$ in the link diagram when restricted to positive $3$-braids or to alternating $3$-braids.

choices.label: C
choices.text: At least one of the two algorithms (the scanning algorithm or the divide-and-conquer algorithm of \cite{MR2320156}) runs in exponential time with respect to the number of crossings in the link diagram, even when restricted to positive $3$-braids or to alternating $3$-braids.

choices.label: D
choices.text: For link diagrams restricted to positive $3$-braids or to alternating $3$-braids, both the scanning algorithm and the divide-and-conquer algorithm of \cite{MR2320156} run in polynomial time in the number of crossings $c$ (i.e. $O(c^k)$ for some fixed $k$).

choices.label: E
choices.text: Even when restricted to positive $3$-braids or to alternating $3$-braids, exactly one of the two algorithms (either the scanning algorithm or the divide-and-conquer algorithm of \cite{MR2320156}) runs in exponential time in the number of crossings, while the other runs in polynomial time.

[H\"older regularity]\label{thm:holder}
Let $u$ be a locally bounded weak solution of the first equation in \eqref{1.1}. 
Then $u$ is locally H\"older continuous in $\mathbb{R}^N \times (0,T]$. 
More precisely, there exist constants $\gamma>0$ and $\alpha \in (0,1)$, depending only on the data, such that for every compact set ${\mathcal{K}} \subset \mathbb{R}^N$,
\[
|u(x_1,t_1) - u(x_2,t_2)| \leq 
\gamma \Big( |x_1-x_2| + \|u\|_\infty^{\tfrac{m-1}{2}} |t_1-t_2|^{1/2} \Big)^{\alpha},
\]
for all $(x_1,t_1), (x_2,t_2) \in {\mathcal K} \times (0,T]$.
theorem.label: thm:holder

theorem.label: MT

sketch:
They prove Theorem~\ref{MT} by “a mixture between Kenig-Ponce-Vega stability type estimates, and the numerical properties ensured by the hypotheses (H1)-(H2)-(H3),” following the method of \cite{ACFMV24} (for 1D NLS), with the main added difficulty being “to establish the correct functional setting to prove stability estimates.” The stability theorem “relies on combining the nonlinear stability framework of Kenig, Ponce, and Vega (KPV) with a rigorous analysis of the residual minimization principle underlying physics-informed neural networks (PINNs).”

Starting from a given neural approximation $u_{\mathrm{DNN},\#}$ that minimizes the residual functional
\[
\mathcal E_k[u_{\mathrm{DNN},\#}] = \partial_t u_{\mathrm{DNN},\#} + \partial_x^3 u_{\mathrm{DNN},\#} + \partial_x(u_{\mathrm{DNN},\#}^k),
\]
(and “other related functionals,” in particular one “minimizing the linear evolution”), they view $\mathcal E_k[u_{\mathrm{DNN},\#}]$ as defining an “approximate solution” and as a nonlinear operator that “will induce an associated functional setting.” Using “the Duhamel formulation and dispersive linear estimates,” the error $w=u-u_{\mathrm{DNN},\#}$ satisfies “an integral inequality controlled by the norms introduced in KPV.” Under “small initial discrepancy and small residual (H2)--(H3),” they obtain “a Gronwall-type estimate leading to explicit and quantitative error bounds,” namely
\[
\|w\|_{Y_{k,s}} \lesssim C(A,\tilde A,L)\,\varepsilon.
\]
Here $Y_{k,s}$ is “the functional setting adapted to each gKdV model,” built from \eqref{eq:Y2s_norm}-\eqref{eq:Y5s_norm} for regularity $s>s_k$ and nonlinearity power $k$. Finally, this global-in-space functional control “will reduce to \eqref{eq:MT1}-\eqref{eq:MT3} after a suitable localization,” yielding the stated bounds for $u-u_{\mathrm{DNN},\#}$ (and for $\partial_x(u^k-u_{\mathrm{DNN},\#}^k)$) on $I\times[-R,R]$.

mcq.question:
Fix \(k\in\{2,3,4,5\}\). Assume \(s\ge s_k\) if \(k\in\{3,4,5\}\) and \(s>s_k\) if \(k=2\). Let \(u_0\in H^s(\mathbb R)\) satisfy (H1). Fix numbers \(A,\widetilde A,L>0\) and take \(0<\varepsilon<\varepsilon_1\) sufficiently small. Let \(u_{\mathrm{DNN},\#}\) be a DNN satisfying (H2)–(H3). For the generalized KdV equation
\[
\partial_t u+\partial_{xxx}u=\mu\,\partial_x(u^k)\qquad (t,x)\in\mathbb R\times\mathbb R,
\]
posed on \(I\times\mathbb R\) with initial datum \(u(0)=u_0\), what is the strongest quantitative conclusion (existence and bounds) that is guaranteed under these assumptions?

correct_choice.label: A
correct_choice.text:
There exists a solution \(u\in C(I;H^s(\mathbb R))\cap Y_{k,s}(I\times\mathbb R)\) to \(\partial_t u+\partial_{xxx}u=\mu\,\partial_x(u^k)\) on \(I\times\mathbb R\) with initial datum \(u(0)=u_0\) such that, for all sufficiently large \(R>0\),
\[
\|u-u_{\mathrm{DNN},\#}\|_{Y_{k,s}(I\times[-R,R])}\le C(A,\widetilde A,L)\,\varepsilon,
\]
\[
\|\partial_x(u^k-u_{\mathrm{DNN},\#}^k)\|_{L_x^2L_t^2(I\times[-R,R])}\le C(A,\widetilde A,L)\,\varepsilon,
\]
and
\[
\|u-u_{\mathrm{DNN},\#}\|_{L_t^{\infty}H_x^s(I\times[-R,R])}\le C(A,\widetilde A,L).
\]
